body:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector swap to the aten->custom path I'm seeing a clear p99 spike for short sequences and tiny microbatches. p50 looks fine, p95 up a bit, p99 jumps a lot.
maya: Repro case: seq_len <= 128, microbatch sizes 1-3 (most traffic is 1). Saw this on both g5x and a100 pools.
ian: Which scheduler params are you running on the canary? max_batch_tokens / max_wait_ms / max_batch_size?
maya: Canary config right now:
```
model: redwood-7b-v1
max_batch_tokens: 1024
max_wait_ms: 3
max_batch_size: 8
kv_cache_prefix_ttl_ms: 50
```
maya: Quick profiling (from the canary trace):
```
p50: 28ms
p95: 62ms
p99: 142ms
observed kernel-switch cost (aten->custom): ~12ms per microbatch
kv_hit_rate: 12% prefix hits
queue_delay median: 1.8ms, tail: 9.4ms
```
maya: Full trace uploaded to dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/1865432100
ian: Hmm. Two likely contributors: 1) kernel-selection overhead that doesn't amortize for single-request microbatches, 2) low prefix KV hit-rate so we rebuild a lot of KV state. Both amplify tail latency.
ian: Can you try bumping max_wait_ms to 8ms to allow slightly larger microbatches and see impact on p99? Also try increasing kv_cache_prefix_ttl_ms to 200ms so warm prefixes stick around longer.
benchbot: quick smoke run completed:
- baseline (max_wait_ms=3, kv_ttl=50): p99=142ms, qps=110
- test (max_wait_ms=8, kv_ttl=200): p99=88ms, qps=108
(note: throughput drop ~1.8%) :eyes:
maya: Benchbot result matches my local runs. p99 halves, p95 also improves. throughput loss negligible for our SLO targets.
maya: However, function-level profiler still shows ~9-11ms added when switching kernels on cold microbatches.
tj: If kernel-selection overhead is fixed cost per microbatch, two levers: a) reduce microbatch frequency (raise max_wait_ms or increase max_batch_tokens so more requests aggregate), b) avoid switching kernels on the hot path (prefer a single compatible kernel for short seqs).
tj: We should test a heuristic: prefer 'custom' kernel only when batch_tokens >= 512; otherwise stick with aten path. That avoids switching for tiny microbatches. Worth a quick canary.
ian: Agreed. Also try increasing batch token cap to 2048 so a single request with long context doesn't artificially force small batches for later arrivals.
maya: I'll spin 3 short experiments for 30m each:
- sweep A: max_wait_ms=[3,8,15] (kv_ttl=50)
- sweep B: max_batch_tokens=[1024,2048,4096] (max_wait_ms=3)
- sweep C: kernel-selection-threshold: prefer custom when batch_tokens>=512 + kv_ttl=[50,200]
ops-bot: Scheduled experiments:
- exp_id=exp-1865432100-a window=30m params={max_wait_ms:[3,8,15],kv_ttl_ms:50}
- exp_id=exp-1865432100-b window=30m params={max_batch_tokens:[1024,2048,4096],max_wait_ms:3}
- exp_id=exp-1865432100-c window=30m params={kernel_threshold_tokens:512,kv_ttl_ms:[50,200]}
ops-bot: Canary rollout policy: traffic slice=5% per variation, abort on p99 increase >10% for 3 consecutive windows.
maya: I'll monitor live traces and post results. First run (max_wait_ms=8) is on now.
benchbot: live quick snapshot after 10m (max_wait_ms=8): p50=30ms p95=58ms p99=90ms kv_hit_rate bumped to 28% during warmup.
ian: If kv hit rate improves with slightly longer wait, that suggests requests are aligning such that prefix reuse occurs — good sign.
tj: If we get consistent wins, we can make default max_wait_ms 8ms for gen endpoints with seq <=256 and tiny microbatch defaults. We'll need doc and per-model tuning.
maya: Next steps: run all experiments, collect p50/p95/p99, qps, and KV hit-rate. I'll create a short perf note and PR for the heuristic if sweep C is positive. tagging @tj for kernel heuristics work.
maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
